items.hook: The Odd Women is an 1893 novel by the English novelist George Gissing.
items.body: Its themes are the role of women in society, marriage, morals and the early feminist movement. Bring it up somewhere. Watch the reaction.

items.hook: ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ sets 10-day North American box office record
items.body: A24 reports best limited opening of the year for ‘Tony’. ’Teenage Sex And Death At Camp Miasma’ opens well for Mubi.

items.hook: Cement is a socialist realism novel by Soviet and Russian writer Fyodor Gladkov (1883–1958).
items.body: Published in 1925, the book is arguably the first in Soviet socialist realist literature to depict the struggles of post-Revolutionary reconstruction. One of those things you can't un-know.

items.hook: The Big Clock is a 1948 American film noir thriller directed by John Farrow and adapted by novelist-screenwriter Jonathan Latimer from the 1946 novel of the same title by Kenneth Fearing.
items.body: The Big Clock stars Ray Milland and Charles Laughton, with Maureen O'Sullivan, George Macready, Rita Johnson and Elsa Lanchester. Worth a quiet trip down the rabbit hole.

items.hook: Drought and heat push Europe’s power grid to breaking point
items.body: High temperatures and low water levels have forced several countries to shut down nuclear reactors just as citizens turn up their air conditioning, forcing energy prices to spike and raising the threat of blackouts

items.hook: Could geoengineering ‘ice arches’ help preserve Arctic sea ice?
items.body: Researchers are investigating whether artificially thickening ice blockages between Canada and Greenland could prevent huge amounts of sea ice from flowing south to melt

items.hook: "The Case of the Stick" is an 1891 short story by Brazilian writer Joaquim Maria Machado de Assis, published first in the Gazeta de Notícias and republished in the book Páginas Recolhidas.
items.body: It is an ironic depiction of slavery in Brazil and selfishness. Bring it up somewhere. Watch the reaction.

items.hook: The Grantville Gazette is the first of a series of professionally selected and edited paid fan fiction anthologies set within the 1632 series inspired by Eric Flint's novel 1632.
items.body: The electronically published the Grantville Gazettes, which were reaching long novel length with regularity, had make up the majority of the series in terms of words in print. One of those things you can't un-know.

items.hook: SpaceX crash site on moon revealed by South Korean orbiter
items.body: An out-of-control SpaceX rocket that crashed into the moon earlier this week did, in fact, leave an impact crater, according to images from a Korea AeroSpace Administration lunar orbiter that caught before-and-after photographs
